prompt:
I need the front end for Tripfold. A home tool for families to put together printable trip booklets (daily plans, photos, activities and notes) for kids or relatives who are going on a journey.

Who's using it: Joan Whitaker, 67, a retired librarian who is taking her grandchildren Ava (10) and Leo (7) on a five-day train trip to Glacier National Park next summer while their parents stay home. She's handy with a computer but no designer. She wants something the kids can hold, write in and keep.

What they're doing right now: She had a 16-page booklet nearly finished when the family swapped the Day 3 hike to Avalanche Lake for a boat tour on Lake McDonald, because Leo is too young for the hike length. She's moving pages and blocks around: replacing the hike page with a boat tour page, shrinking the packing checklist so a train-spotting bingo still fits, and moving her photo of the kids' mother at the same lodge in 1994 next to the page about arriving there. The booklet has to come out to exactly 16 pages so it prints and folds as a letter-size booklet, and she wants Leo's pages to use larger text than Ava's.

What's in the system at this point: Trip: Chicago Union Station to West Glacier on the Empire Builder, departing Jul 12, 2027, 3 nights at Lake McDonald Lodge, returning Jul 17. The booklet has 16 pages: cover, 'Meet the Train', one page per day (5), a packing checklist, train-spotting bingo with 16 squares, a 'Wildlife We Saw' tally (mountain goat, bighorn sheep, bald eagle, marmot, moose), two journal pages, a postcard pocket page, an emergency contacts page and a back cover. 22 photos uploaded, including 1994_lodge_mom.jpg. Each page is made of text blocks, images, checkboxes and the route stops (Milwaukee, St. Paul, Minot, Havre, Shelby, East Glacier, West Glacier). The boat tour has a 10:00 departure and 1.5-hour duration. Two pages are currently over capacity.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
